title: How a kiln turns clay into ceramic
examples: What happens to clay in a kiln?
Why do pots crack in the kiln?

explain.say: Soft clay is made of tiny flat mineral plates with water between them. A kiln heats it slowly at first, so leftover water can steam out gently instead of cracking or bursting the pot.

draw.text: How a kiln turns clay into ceramic

explain.say: Next, water locked inside the clay crystals is driven off, which changes the clay forever. Around 573 degrees Celsius, quartz grains in the clay suddenly change shape and size, so potters heat gently through that point.

At the top temperature, often 1,000 to 1,300 degrees, some minerals melt into a glassy glue that binds the particles together. This is vitrification, and stoneware and porcelain fired hottest become waterproof.
The kiln then cools slowly so the pot does not crack, especially around 573 degrees again. A glaze, a coating of powdered glass, can be fired on to melt into a smooth, shiny skin.

faq.q: Why can't fired clay turn back into clay?
faq.a: Firing drives out water bound inside the clay minerals and fuses the grains with glassy material. Those chemical changes are permanent, so soaking a fired pot in water does not soften it.
asks: What happens to clay when it is fired?

faq.q: Why do pots crack in the kiln?
faq.a: Pots crack if water turns to steam too fast inside them, if they heat or cool unevenly, or if they pass too quickly through about 573 degrees, where quartz suddenly changes size. Slow, steady firing prevents this.
asks: Why did my pot explode in the kiln?

faq.a: Vitrification means turning partly into glass. At high temperature, some minerals melt and flow between the clay grains, then harden as glass on cooling, making the ceramic dense, strong and less able to soak up water.
A glaze is a coating of finely ground glass-making minerals painted or dipped onto pottery. In the kiln it melts into a smooth, glassy layer that is waterproof, easy to clean and can be any colour.

faq.q: What is the difference between earthenware, stoneware and porcelain?
faq.a: Earthenware is fired cooler, around 1,000 to 1,150 degrees, and stays slightly porous. Stoneware is fired hotter and becomes dense and waterproof. Porcelain uses fine white clay fired hottest and can be so thin that light shines through.

facts: Quartz changes crystal form at 573 °C with a sudden change in volume, a common cause of cracking during firing.
The Venus of Dolní Věstonice, made around 26,000 years ago, is among the oldest known fired ceramic objects.

quiz.say: Why does a potter heat a kiln slowly at the start?

options.show: Water can escape without cracking the pots
options.say: Water can escape without cracking the pots

quiz.why: Water left in the clay would boil into steam and crack or burst the pot if heated too fast.

wrong.1: Glaze melts at the top temperature; slow early heating protects against steam.
wrong.2: The kiln uses energy throughout; slow heating is about the clay.
